## Verified first

Built clean with `--all-features` and with `--no-default-features --features unstable-testing`. All 8 `network::connection_pool::tests` pass under `--features metrics` (`many_connections` fails without a live cluster — pre-existing, unrelated).

The core fix is sound. I specifically checked for double-decrement between the three new `decrement_total_connections` call sites and `remove_connection`: it can't happen, because `remove_connection` matches by `Arc::ptr_eq` and a cleared connection is no longer in `conns`/`excess_connections`, so the `wait_for_error` event that fires afterwards falls through to the "already removed" path. Underflow is also not reachable — every connection in those vectors was `inc_total_connections`'d by `count_in_metrics`.

## Findings

**1. MEDIUM — `scylla/src/network/connection_pool.rs:1006` — excess shard-aware connection is discarded without decrementing `total_connections`**
This is the fourth discard site in `handle_ready_connection`, and the PR fixed the other three but not this one. In the `else if evt.requested_shard.is_some()` arm, `connection` is never moved into an `Arc` and never stored — it is dropped at the end of the match arm — yet `count_in_metrics` (`:1051`) already incremented the gauge when it was opened. Under the source-port-rewriting scenario the branch's own comment describes, every such connection permanently inflates `total_connections`. Same bug class the PR exists to fix, in the same function it rewrote.

**2. MEDIUM — `scylla/src/network/connection_pool.rs:696` (and `:191`) — pool teardown leaks the entire gauge**
When `NodeConnectionPool` is dropped, `_refiller_handle: Arc<RemoteHandle<()>>` cancels the refiller; `run()` also returns here when the keyspace channel closes. Either way `self.conns` and `self.excess_connections` are dropped with no decrement, so removing a node from the cluster or dropping the session inflates `total_connections` forever. The new test actually encodes this as expected behaviour: `:2011` asserts the gauge is still `1` after `worker.await` returned and the refiller (holding that connection) was dropped.

**3. LOW-MEDIUM — `scylla/src/network/connection_pool.rs:903` — keyspace failure demoted from `warn!` to `debug!` at exactly the point it became fatal**
Previously a failed `USE` logged at `warn!` and the connection was still used, so the session kept working. Now the connection is discarded and the pool can go `Broken`, but the only record is at `debug!`. An operator whose keyspace was dropped server-side sees a node that silently reconnects forever with growing backoff and nothing above debug level explaining why.

**4. LOW-MEDIUM — validation gap: none of the three new metrics tests ran under the commands in the PR description**
`scylla/Cargo.toml:35` is `default = []`, and the new tests are gated at `:1866`, `:1942`, `:1970` (plus the helper at `:1854`). Neither `cargo test -p scylla --lib network::connection_pool::tests::keyspace_setup_failure` nor `cargo check -p scylla --lib` enables `metrics`, so those tests were neither compiled nor executed by the stated validation. They do pass with `--features metrics` — the claim just isn't backed by the commands listed.

**5. LOW — PR description covers 1 of 4 commits**
`de164845`, `0d91aa54`, `617139df` (metrics balancing on pool clear, plus its tests) are not mentioned anywhere in the description or the checklist. A reviewer reading the description alone would treat the `maybe_reshard` / excess-clear metric changes as unexplained drive-by edits.

**6. NIT — `scylla/src/network/connection_pool.rs:1360` — `decrement_total_connections` does N separate `fetch_sub(1)`**
`total_connections` is read concurrently through the public `Metrics::get_total_connections()`, so a scrape landing mid-loop reports a value that never corresponded to any real state. A single `fetch_sub(count)` would be atomic and cheaper; it needs a `dec_total_connections_by` in both `metrics.rs` and `metrics_noop.rs`.

**7. NIT — `scylla/src/network/connection_pool.rs:1499` — unit test builds an event shape production never emits**
`ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace` is only ever produced by `start_setting_keyspace_for_connection`, which always sets `keyspace_name: Some(..)` (`:1347`); the test pairs it with `None`, and also sets `requested_shard: Some(..)`, which the keyspace branch never reads. Harmless now, but the test wouldn't catch a regression that made the branch depend on either field.

**8. INFO — sharder discovery is now deferred by one `USE` round-trip**
Moving the keyspace check ahead of `maybe_reshard` (`:910`) means that when `current_keyspace` is set, the first connection's sharding info and shard-aware port aren't adopted until its `USE` completes. Intentional and asserted by `keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state`, but it does mean the refill immediately following a `use_keyspace` cannot use the shard-aware port.

**9. INFO — non-transient `USE` failure now takes the node fully down rather than degrading it**
Before, a connection with a failed `USE` still filled the pool. Now it is discarded, so a keyspace dropped server-side leaves every pool empty, publishes `MaybePoolConnections::Broken(ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError(..))`, and emits `ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost` for every node. That is the intended trade-off of the fix, but it converts a degraded-but-usable session into a fully-down cluster and deserves an explicit line in the description.
